records.c: The match's player count, kept in the program's first byte: 2 for two players, 1 when the computer plays player one, 0 in the demo. The file loads with 1.
Space Hockey's entry, jumped to by the resident event loader at $0970: silences the SID (sid_init $661B) and shows the event's title screen through the resident $C540 (A = 2).

Banks the KERNAL and BASIC ROMs out (I/O stays), points the NMI vector at nmi_rti ($2DE6) and the IRQ vector at irq_entry ($0F9E), stops CIA 1's timer interrupt and turns on the raster interrupt, blanks the screen, picks video bank 1 ($4000-$7FFF) with the screen matrix at $4000 and the bitmap and character set at $6000, sets the sprite colours (puck and its scanner dot white, player one light red, player two green, the scanner's window blue), draws the screen ($126D) and the floor ($26F5). In the demo, the score and round are left alone; otherwise round 1 and both scores 0.
Sets the clock to 60.00 seconds ($0F91 = $60, $0F90 = 0), draws the clock, the scores and the round number, and turns the screen on.

The top of each round: shows "DEMO MODE" in the demo, freezes play ($267C = 1), resets the puck's daze ($2678-$267A), the goal flag and the timers, redraws the clock and round, puts the puck and the players on their spots ($23B2), then beams in player one (sprites 1, 5 and 7), player two (adding 2 and 6) and the puck (all eight) with $2568, fifty frames apart. In the demo a fire press during this starts a match ($0C9D).

Starts the round: the puck sets off diagonally at speed $0100 in a random direction (two random bits for left or right and up or down), play is unfrozen, the clock starts ($0F92 = 1), both players are held for 10 frames ($2681, $2682) and the starting sound plays (effect 7).
The main loop. In the demo, a fire press (fire_device $2388) goes to choose_players and a new match ($0C9D); when the round is over ($267B) it goes to round_over, otherwise to frame_work ($0D00).
A fire press in the demo: asks who is playing (choose_players $24BE) and starts the match from the top ($0B8E).

The round has ended: freezes play, plays effect 4 and redraws the clock. The demo goes straight on to another round; a match goes to the next round while there are rounds left (round $2676 under 4) and to match_over after round 4.

After the fourth round, or an overtime round: with the scores level, shows "OVERTIME" and plays another round ($0CE8). Otherwise shows "GAME OVER", keeps the scores for the records ($0F04), waits 256 frames and goes back to the demo ($2677 = $FF, players = 0).
Adds one to the round number (BCD), sets the clock back to 60 seconds, waits 40 frames and starts the round.

One pass of the main loop while play runs: copies the three objects' positions to the drawing copies ($2691-$269C), places the scanner dots ($188A), draws the clock, chooses the puck's frame ($2289), moves the view ($26BB, $2759) and places the field sprites ($1820). After a goal it runs goal_scored and either restarts the round or, with the clock at zero, ends it; otherwise reads the controls ($1DF5) and tests the three pairs for a collision ($20B9: puck and player one, puck and player two, the two players).

Something fell into a black hole. Outside the demo the score changes: the puck in the right-hand hole gives player one 3, in the left-hand hole player two 3 ($0D9B); a player who fell in gives the other player 1. Then redraws the scores and, for 200 frames, lets the view follow the object that fell in, before playing effect 3 and the swallowing animation.

The swallowing animation: plays animation 3 (or 2 for the puck, at $0E56) on the object that fell in, a frame every five frames, moving it $C0 a step further into the hole, until the animation ends; then waits 40 frames and clears the goal flag.
goal_scored's frame count (200 frames).
The scores kept for the records: the player count when the computer played ($0F01), player one's score ($0F02) and player two's ($0F03), $FF when there is none.
Player one's score for the records, $FF for none.
Player two's score for the records, $FF for none.
At the end of a match, copies the scores to $0F02 and $0F03 for the records: player one's only when two people played, player two's always, and the player count to $0F01 when it was not 2.
Draws the two scores as seven-segment digits: player one's ($26B9) at $4052 and $4054, player two's ($26BA) at $4072 and $4074.
Draws the round number ($2676) as one seven-segment digit at $4063.
The round clock in BCD: hundredths ($0F90) and seconds ($0F91), counting down from 60.00.
The clock's seconds, BCD.
Whether the clock runs (1) or is stopped (0).
A spare byte, then the band number ($0F94, 0 to 3) and the raster line's ninth bit for the next band ($0F95).
The band number, 0 to 3.
The next band's raster ninth bit, ORed into $D011.
The four bands' raster lines and ninth bits: $69 (the top of the field), $B1, $F2 (the message line) and 256 (the bottom).
Each band's ninth raster bit, read as band_lines + 1: $80 for line 256.

The raster interrupt, reached through the RAM vector at $FFFE: saves A, X and Y at $0B-$0D, sends a BRK to the resident code at $0810, and otherwise jumps to the handler for this band (the JMP at $0FAD, whose operand the last interrupt set).
The BRK way out: jumps to the resident code at $0810.
The JMP to the current band's handler; its operand ($0FAE) is rewritten from band_handlers.
band_jump's operand, low byte: the current band handler's address.
band_jump's operand, high byte.
The four band handlers' addresses: band_field ($11D1), band_pause ($1176), band_message ($120F) and band_frame ($0FB8).
The high bytes of band_handlers.

The band handler at line 256, once a frame: checks RUN/STOP ($2DE7). Unless play is frozen ($267C), counts down both players' brake and stun timers ($267F, $2681) and the computer's thinking delay ($2684), slows every object by $10 every 17 frames, runs the black holes' pull ($1A51), and moves each object by its speed. A braking player stops dead; an object reaching the left or right wall inside the hole's rows falls in (hole_test $2231), otherwise every wall bounces it back with effect 1 (bounce $11BA). Takes 2 hundredths off the running clock (one second in 50 frames), ending the round at zero.

The part of band_frame that runs even while play is frozen: counts down the puck's animation delay ($2683), the daze timer ($2679, which clears the dazed flag $2678 at zero), the message timers ($2A4A, $2A4B); every 25 frames flashes the message cursor (character $12 at $6090 inverted); moves the message line ($2993), the black hole sprite ($2025) and the sound ($6581, unless an effect is being started), then sets the screen back to multicolour and acknowledges the interrupt.
Frames until the message cursor flashes again (25).

The band handler at line $B1: in a match, reads the Commodore key (keyboard row 7, column 5), and on each new press toggles the pause ($267C) with "GAME PAUSED" or "GAME RESTORED". The manual does not mention it.
The Commodore key's state at the last look, so that holding it toggles the pause only once.
An object hit a wall: plays effect 1; a player is stunned for 20 frames ($2681), the puck plays animation 1.
Frames until every object is slowed again (17).

The band handler at line $69, the top of the field: waits along a slide of NOPs, turns multicolour off, sets the field sprites' shapes (the puck $12, the players $13 and $14, the black hole $20AF) and turns bitmap mode on.
The band handler at line $F2, the message line: points sprites 0 to 3 at the empty shape $11 and turns bitmap mode off, so the last row shows as text.

Ends every band handler: acknowledges the raster interrupt, counts frames for the random numbers ($2385), moves to the next band, sets its raster line and ninth bit and the handler the next interrupt jumps to, restores A, X and Y and returns from the interrupt.

Clears the field's bitmap ($68C0-$7DFF), copies the screen matrix from $1320 to $4000 and colour RAM from $1708, sets the colours (grey background and border, light grey and dark grey for multicolour), clears the message line and points the scanner sprites at shapes $12 and $13.
The screen matrix draw_screen copies to $4000: the panel's characters for rows 0 to 6 (the scores, the scanner's frame, the round number and the clock),
The second page of screen_data, copied to $4100: the panel's bottom rows and the field's top rows, blue.
then the field's colours for rows 7 to 23, one byte a cell in bitmap mode (blue $06 for the floor), and the message line.
The third page of screen_data, copied to $4200: more of the field's colours.
The last page of screen_data, copied to $4300: the field's bottom rows, the white row under it, the message line and bytes over the sprite pointers, which draw_screen then sets.
The colour RAM draw_screen copies to $D800: the panel's colours. It copies 512 bytes, so the rows below the panel get the bytes of the program that follows, which the bitmap's rows never read.
The second page colour_data copies, to $D900: from $1820 these are the program's own bytes.

Places the field sprites for the puck, player one and player two from the drawing copies: an object within $58 units across and $2A down of the view's corner ($28C4, $28C3) is drawn there, four pixels a unit with the low byte's top two bits added; one outside it is hidden (Y = 0).
The sprites' ninth X bits (1, 2, 4) and their opposites ($FE, $FD, $FB) for place_sprites.
The masks that clear the sprites' ninth X bits: $FE, $FD, $FB.
Places the scanner's dots (sprites 4 to 6) at each object's position divided by four, and its window (sprite 7) at the view's corner.
When the view reaches the bottom wall, draws row 22 of the field white ($11); wall_bottom_off ($18D0) puts it back to blue when the view moves up.
Puts row 22 back to blue when the view leaves the bottom wall, keeping the walls' corner cells if a hole column is drawn.
Whether the bottom wall's row is drawn (bit 7 set).
The top wall's row (row 7, $4118), drawn and removed as wall_bottom does; wall_top_off at $1909.
Puts row 7 back to blue when the view leaves the top wall.
Whether the top wall's row is drawn.

When the view reaches the left wall, draws its column (column 0 of the field) in white, with the black hole's rows in dark grey ($BB) where the view's rows cover $33-$4B; hole_left_off ($1961) puts it back to blue.
Puts column 0 back to blue when the view leaves the left wall.
Whether the left wall's column is drawn.
The right wall's column (column 39), drawn and removed as hole_left does; hole_right_off at $19CF.
Puts column 39 back to blue when the view leaves the right wall.
Whether the right wall's column is drawn.
One cell of a wall's column: dark grey ($BB) inside the black hole's rows ($33 to $4B), white ($11) outside, stepping the row counter $1A24 by two.
The row counter wall_colour steps.
The same as wall_colour, for the right-hand column.
Frames until the next pull (8).
Each object's pull across ($1A3F), down ($1A45) and their directions ($1A4B), two bytes an object: puck, player one, player two.
Each object's pull down, two bytes an object.
Each object's pull direction across ($FF left), two bytes an object.
Each object's pull direction down ($FF up), read as pull_x's directions + 1.

Every eight frames, for each object: works out the pull where it stands (pull_at $1B15) and adds it to its speed when it pulls the way the object moves, at most $0100; against it, takes it off, and once the speed is spent turns the object round.

The pull on object X: its place on the floor's 16 x 8 grid (the high byte of X over 16, plus the high byte of Y's top three bits) picks a byte in the pull tables ($1BF5 across, $1CF5 down): bit 7 the direction, the rest the strength, eight times over and at most $30. The puck is pushed the other way unless it is dazed ($2678). For the players it adds their own push ($26AF-$26B6), which nothing sets.
pull_at's work byte.

The pull across for each square of the floor, sixteen across and eight down (only the first 128 bytes are read): bit 7 set pulls left, clear right, with strength 1 to 3. Each half pulls towards its own wall, hardest in the rows of the black hole.
The second half of pull_across, which pull_at never reads.
The pull up or down for each square: bit 7 set up, clear down. Squares above the hole's rows pull down and those below pull up, so everything drifts towards a hole.
The second half of pull_down, which pull_at never reads.

Reads both players' controls: player one from the computer (think $1EC1) unless two people play, player two from the computer in the demo ($1F90). Fire brakes for five frames (shape $15); a stunned player shows shape $2E; otherwise the shape comes from the direction held (player_shapes $1EB1). A player not stunned moves at speed $0100 in each direction held and stops in a direction not held.
The players' shapes for each joystick direction (up, down, left, right and the diagonals); $14 when no direction is held.

The computer's players, thinking every 13 frames ($2684). One thought in thirty, both wander in a random direction, sometimes with fire. Otherwise player one plays towards the right-hand hole: with the puck at least 2 units to its right, it moves right when within 6 rows of the puck's height and up or down towards it when not; otherwise it heads back left, diagonally towards the puck's height when more than 10 rows away and straight left when nearer, except near the left wall (X under $0A), where it moves right. A stunned player one sometimes brakes. Player two's choice ($1F94) is kept at $1F7B.
Player one's chosen direction ($1F79), the count to the next wander ($1F7A) and player two's direction ($1F7B).
Thoughts to the next wander.
Player two's direction, from think.
Banks I/O in with the ROMs out ($01 = %xx1xxx01); A is kept.
Banks I/O out as well, leaving all RAM; A is kept.
Player two's controls in the demo: the direction think chose.
The computer's player two, the mirror image of player one: it plays towards the left-hand hole, moving left when within 5 rows of the puck's height.
Returns player two's last direction ($2024). Nothing calls it: think keeps player two's choice at $1F7B instead.

Player two's choice when it is not wandering: right of the puck and level with it, left; not level, up or down towards it; past the puck, back to the right, diagonally when more than 10 rows away, unless near the right wall (X $F6 or more).
Player two's chosen direction.

The black hole: steps its shape every four frames through $20B0, and while the view is at the left or right end shows sprite 3, double size, at that wall, at the height of the hole's rows; elsewhere it is hidden.

The black hole's place in its shape list ($20AD), its frame count ($20AE), its shape ($20AF), the shapes ($2F to $33, $20B0, ended by $FF), its colour place ($20B6) and its colour list ($20B7: white, ended by $FF).
Frames to the black hole's next shape.
The black hole's shape, which band_field gives sprite 3.
The black hole's shapes: $2F to $33, then $FF to start again.
The black hole's place in its colour list.
The black hole's colours: white, then $FF to start again.

Tests objects X and Y for a hit: when they are within 6 units each way, the 6 x 6 table at $21C3 says whether they touch, and the tables at $21E7 and $220B give the speed across and down. Both take that speed, in opposite directions. A hit on the puck plays effect 2 and animation 0 and dazes the puck ($219F); two players colliding plays effect 6. The player hit is stunned for 20 frames.
Dazes the puck for $267A frames and, unless it was dazed already, makes the next daze 4 frames longer, up to 150.
collide's saved X.
For each pair of distances (across, down, 0 to 5), $FF when the two objects touch.
The speed across the hit gives, for each pair of distances.
The speed down the hit gives, for each pair of distances.
collide's distances across ($222F) and down ($2230).
collide's distance down.

An object at the left or right wall: when its Y is within $36 to $4A it has fallen in. Puts it in the hole ($04C0 or $FCC0), stops it, freezes play and the clock, and records which object it was ($267E) with the goal flag $267D. Returns carry set when it fell in.
Waits for the raster to pass line 256: one frame.

Every five frames, picks the puck's shape: the next frame of its animation if one plays, $1D while it is dazed, $10 while it stands still, and otherwise the way it faces, from its larger speed: $16 down, $17 up, $18 right, $19 left.
puck_shape's halved speeds across and down.
puck_shape's halved speed down.
Whether the puck's animation plays ($22FD), its frame list ($22FE) and its place in it ($2300).
The puck animation's frame list, low byte.
The puck animation's frame list, high byte.
The puck animation's place in its list.
Returns the next frame of the puck's animation, or $FF (minus) when it has ended.
Starts the puck's animation A (0 to 3) from anim_table.
anim_start's saved Y.
The four animations' frame lists: 0 hit, 1 bounce, 2 swallowed puck, 3 swallowed player.
The high bytes of anim_table.
The frames, each list ended by $FF.
Animation 1, the bounce: frames $1A, $1A.
Animation 2, the puck swallowed: frames $1D and $27 to $2A, then $11 (empty).
Animation 3, a player swallowed: frames $14 and $2B to $2D, $2A, then $11 (empty).
Waits X frames.
A random byte: the next byte of the page that $2386 points into, exclusive-ORed with the frame counter $2385.
random's saved Y, the frame counter it mixes in ($2385) and its pointer ($2386).
The frame counter random mixes in.
random's pointer, low byte, which steps through its page.
random's pointer, high byte: page $0B, the program's own code.

Reads the three fire buttons: the up-arrow key (keyboard row 6, column 6), joystick one's fire and joystick two's fire. Returns carry set and A = 0, 1 or 2 for the first one held, carry clear when none is.

Stops all three objects and puts them on their spots (the puck at $81, player one at $78, player two at $8A, all at height $41), leaves only the scanner's window on, and lets the view settle on the puck over 100 frames.
reset_places's frame count.

Reads player one's controls from the device it chose ($2566); read_p2 ($2453) reads player two's from $2567. Joystick one or two as the port reads, the keyboard through read_keys, inverted so that a 1 bit is a direction or fire held.
Reads player two's controls from the device it chose ($2567).

Reads the keyboard player's controls into the joystick's bit pattern: @ up (bit 0), : down (bit 1), H left (bit 2), K right (bit 3) and the up-arrow key fire (bit 4), from keyboard rows 5, 3, 4 and 6. The manual gives K as left and H as right.
read_keys's work byte.

Asks who plays: "PLAYER ONE PRESS FIRE" beams player one in until a fire press, then "PLAYER TWO PRESS FIRE" beams player two in. The keyboard with joystick two is refused ("KEYBOARD AND JOYSTICK TWO NOT ALLOWED"). The same device for both makes it a one-player game against the computer ("PLAYER ONE IS COMPUTER", players 1), two devices a two-player game ("TWO PLAYER GAME", players 2). Ends the demo.
The device each player chose: 0 keyboard, 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two.
The device player two chose: 0 keyboard, 1 joystick one, 2 joystick two.
Beams a sprite in: over X frames, builds shape A into the spare shape at $4780 a few random bits at a time, thinner masks first ($88, then $AA), with effect 5; Y is the sprite enable mask to set.
The operand of beam_in's AND, rewritten with shape A's address.
The high byte of beam_in's source shape address.
The mask's operand, rotated a bit each step so the pattern moves.
beam_in's thresholds: half and three quarters of the steps.
beam_in's three-quarter threshold.
Beams a sprite out, the reverse of beam_in.
The operand of beam_out's AND, rewritten with the shape's address.
The high byte of beam_out's source shape address.
beam_out's rotating mask.
beam_out's thresholds.
beam_out's quarter threshold.
Set while choose_players asks for fire, so the message line holds its message.
The round number in BCD, 1 to 4 and on into overtime.
$FF in the demo, 0 in a match.
$FF while the puck is dazed, its timer ($2679) and the next daze's length ($267A).
Frames left of the puck's daze.
The next daze's length, from 10 up to 150.
Set when the clock reaches zero.
Play is frozen: at the start of a round, after a goal, during a hit and while paused.
Set when something fell into a hole; $267E says which: 0 the puck, 1 player one, 2 player two.
Which object fell in: 0 the puck, 1 player one, 2 player two.
Each player's brake time ($267F, $2680) and stun time ($2681, $2682), in frames.
Player one's stun time, in frames.
Player two's stun time, in frames.
Frames to the puck's next animation frame ($2683) and to the computer's next thought ($2684).
Frames to the computer's next thought.
The three objects' X positions, two bytes each (low, high): puck, player one, player two. The floor runs from 5 to $FD.
The puck's X, high byte: 5 at the left wall, $FD at the right.
Player one's X, low byte.
Player one's X, high byte.
Player two's X, low byte.
Player two's X, high byte.
Their Y positions, from 5 to $7D.
The puck's Y, high byte.
Player one's Y, low byte.
Player one's Y, high byte.
Player two's Y, low byte.
Player two's Y, high byte.
Copies of the positions that place_sprites shifts as it works: X,
The puck's drawing X, high byte, which the view follows.
Player one's drawing X, low byte.
Player one's drawing X, high byte.
Player two's drawing X, low byte.
Player two's drawing X, high byte.
and Y.
The puck's drawing Y, high byte.
Player one's drawing Y, low byte.
Player one's drawing Y, high byte.
Player two's drawing Y, low byte.
Player two's drawing Y, high byte.
The objects' speeds across, two bytes each, at most $0100;
The puck's speed across, high byte.
Player one's speed across, low byte (player two's at $26A1).
Player one's speed across, the high byte, which read_controls sets to 1 or 0 (with Y = 0; player two's with Y = 2).
and down.
The puck's speed down, high byte.
Player one's speed down, low byte.
Player one's speed down, the high byte, which read_controls sets.
Each object's directions, two bytes an object: across ($26A9, $FF left) and down ($26AA, $FF up).
The puck's direction down ($FF up).
Player one's direction across ($FF left).
Player one's direction down, which read_controls sets.
Pushes for the players across and down and their directions, which pull_at adds to the pull; nothing writes them, so they stay 0.
The players' pushes down (nothing writes them).
The directions of the players' pushes across ($26B3) and down ($26B5), never written.
The directions of the players' pushes down, never written.
The players' controls this frame, a 1 bit for each direction or fire held.
Player two's controls.
Player one's score ($26B9) and player two's ($26BA), in BCD.
Player two's score, BCD.

While the view is settled ($27DC not minus), checks that the puck is still inside the middle of the view ($14-$3C across, $06-$1D down from its corner); when it leaves, sets the view following again ($27DC minus).

Draws the floor: copies the starting edges of the floor's bands ($2747) to $28C5, puts the view at the top left (0, 0) and fills in the bands that start on the screen, the first horizontal one ($288F) and the first three vertical ones ($284B). The CPX #$03 has no branch after it, so the loop ends after one horizontal band; the others start below the screen.
The bands' starting edges: twelve vertical ($08 to $F8 across, in four-pixel units) and six horizontal ($18 to $68 down, in four-pixel rows), in pairs, each pair one band.

While the view follows ($27DC minus), moves it one unit a frame towards the puck (its corner at the puck less $29 across and $12 down), scrolling the floor ($27EF, $2805, $281B, $2833) and drawing or clearing the walls and the hole's columns as it reaches or leaves an end; once it is centred on the puck it settles.
Minus while the view follows the puck, 0 once it has settled.
A byte nothing reads.
Redraws whichever hole column is shown after a vertical scroll, through the JMPs at $27E9 (left) and $27EC (right).
Moves the view one unit right, so the floor moves left: takes one off every vertical edge, flipping the four-pixel column at each one still on the screen ($284B).
Moves the view one unit left: flips the column at each edge on the screen and adds one to every vertical edge.
Moves the view one unit up: flips the row at each horizontal edge on the screen ($288F) and adds one to it.
Moves the view one unit down: takes one off each horizontal edge and flips the row at those on the screen.

Flips one four-pixel column of the floor's bitmap (exclusive-OR with $F0 or $0F) from top to bottom, seventeen character rows: A is the column in four-pixel units, its cell's address from $28D7. A band's colour comes from flipping at both its edges, so a band moves by flipping one column at each.
The operand of flip_column's EOR, rewritten with $F0 or $0F for the column's half of the cell.

Flips one four-pixel row of the floor's bitmap across all 40 cells: A is the row, its address from $2927. Where a horizontal band crosses a vertical one the two flips cancel, which draws the chequerboard.
The view's corner on the floor: Y ($28C3, 0 to $5E) and X ($28C4, 0 to $B0).
The view's X, 0 to $B0.
The vertical bands' edges as they stand, twelve bytes, in four-pixel units from the view's left; an edge at $50 or more is off the screen.
The far edge of each vertical band, read as band_edges + 1.
The horizontal bands' edges, six bytes, in four-pixel rows from the view's top; an edge at $22 or more is off the screen.
The far edge of each horizontal band, read as band_rows + 1.
The bitmap address of each of the field's 40 cell columns in its top row ($68C0, $68C8 and on).
The high bytes of column_addrs.
The last columns' addresses.
The bitmap address of each four-pixel row of the field, 34 of them: the top and bottom halves of each character row from $68C0.
The high bytes of row_addrs.
The last row's address.
Starts message A on the message line: points $06 at its text (message_table $2A4C) and sets the line to scroll the old message out (19 steps) before typing the new one in.

Moves the message line on, every second frame: first scrolls the old message off to the left, then types the new one in a character at a time with the cursor (character $12) after it, then holds it ($2A4B). When it has been held, picks the next of the advertising messages from $2A33, skipping "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY" (0) outside the demo; while choose_players asks for fire the line keeps its message.
The order of the advertising messages on the message line, ended by $FF: 0 and 1 to 13, with message 0 ("PRESS FIRE TO PLAY") between the groups.

The message line's place in message_cycle ($2A45), the steps left to scroll out ($2A46), its phase ($2A47: 0 scrolling out, 1 typing, 2 holding), a skip flag ($2A48), the column being typed ($2A49), the frames to the next step ($2A4A) and the hold time ($2A4B).
Steps left to scroll the old message out.
The message line's phase: 0 scrolling out, 1 typing, 2 holding.
Set to skip typing (show_message with $FF).
The message line's column being typed.
Frames to the message line's next step.
Frames to hold the typed message.
The addresses of the 25 messages, numbered from 0.
The high bytes of message_table.
The messages, each ended by $FF, typed on the message line with 0 for a space and the letter's code plus $D2 (so A is $13). Message 0 "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY", 1 "S P A C E   H O C K E Y",
Message 0, "PRESS FIRE TO PLAY", ended by $FF, after ten spaces.

The NMI handler: returns at once, so RESTORE does nothing.
Reads the RUN/STOP key (keyboard row 7, column 7); when it is held, leaves the event (quit_to_menu).

Leaves the event: puts the match's scores into the resident record ($B80A for player one, $B80C for player two, $B812 for the player count) unless both are $FF, calls the resident $B839 with $02 = 1 (this event's number) when $B800 is 0, initialises I/O, RAM, the KERNAL's vectors and the screen editor, and loads HARRY (load_harry $2FEC). If the load fails it prints the disk error and tries again after 200 frames; once it loads, sets $FF to 2 and jumps to the menu at $0E90.
The text quit_to_menu prints when HARRY will not load: clear screen, two returns, "ERROR READING DISK...", two returns, "ENSURE CORRECT DISK IS IN DRIVE", ended by $FF.
The seven-segment pattern of each digit 0 to 9 (and six more), a bit a segment, for seg_digit.

Draws the clock, seconds ($0F91) and hundredths ($0F90), as four seven-segment digits at $4067, $4069, $406C and $406E, and blinks the colon at $4093 and $40BB: hidden while the clock runs and the hundredths read 70 or more ($2F36 remembers which).

Draws one seven-segment digit: A is the segment mask (from $2EAE), X and Y the screen address. Each pair of segments becomes one character code in a 2 x 3 block of cells.

Loads "0:HARRY" (name at $3019) from drive 8 to its own address through the resident fast loader at $0800, reading the drive's status after; returns carry set when the status is anything but 0 or $40 (end of file).
